chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) is treated with Water (H2O)?
questions.explanation: Treating Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) with Water (H2O) yields Acetic acid (CH3COOH) + HCl. Rationale: Water rapidly attacks the highly electrophilic acyl chloride; chloride leaving group is expelled instantly.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) into Benzamide (PhCONH2) + Ammonium chloride?
questions.explanation: To convert Benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) into Benzamide (PhCONH2) + Ammonium chloride, the appropriate reagent is 2 equivalents Ammonia (NH3). Rationale: Ammonia attacks acyl chloride; second equivalent of ammonia neutralizes generated HCl byproduct.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is treated with Acetic anhydride + trace H2SO4?
questions.explanation: Treating Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) with Acetic anhydride + trace H2SO4 yields Acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) + Acetic acid. Rationale: Phenolic hydroxyl group attacks acetic anhydride in a nucleophilic acyl substitution.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Ethyl acetate (CH3COOCH2CH3) into Sodium acetate (CH3COONa) + Ethanol?
questions.explanation: To convert Ethyl acetate (CH3COOCH2CH3) into Sodium acetate (CH3COONa) + Ethanol, the appropriate reagent is Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) in H2O / heat. Rationale: Hydroxide attacks ester carbonyl; irreversible collapse to carboxylate salt drives the reaction to completion.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) is treated with Excess ethanol + catalytic sodium ethoxide?
questions.explanation: Treating Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) with Excess ethanol + catalytic sodium ethoxide yields Ethyl benzoate (PhCOOCH2CH3) + Methanol. Rationale: Ethoxide nucleophile displaces methoxide in an equilibrium driven forward by excess ethanol.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Ethyl butanoate into 1-Butanol + Ethanol?
questions.explanation: To convert Ethyl butanoate into 1-Butanol + Ethanol, the appropriate reagent is 1. LiAlH4 in ether; 2. Aqueous H3O+. Rationale: LiAlH4 reduces the ester through an aldehyde intermediate down to primary alcohol.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. DIBAL-H in toluene (-78°C); 2. H3O+ to yield Butanal + Ethanol as the major product?
questions.explanation: Ethyl butanoate reacts with 1. DIBAL-H in toluene (-78°C); 2. H3O+ to yield Butanal + Ethanol. Rationale: Diisobutylaluminum hydride at -78°C yields a stable hemiacetal intermediate, preventing over-reduction.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) is treated with 1. 2 equivalents CH3MgBr; 2. Aqueous H3O+?
questions.explanation: Treating Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) with 1. 2 equivalents CH3MgBr; 2. Aqueous H3O+ yields 2-Phenyl-2-propanol (3° alcohol) + Methanol. Rationale: First Grignard addition generates a ketone intermediate; immediate second addition constructs tertiary alcohol.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. LiAlH4 in THF; 2. H2O to yield N,N-Dimethylbenzylamine (PhCH2N(CH3)2) as the major product?
questions.explanation: N,N-Dimethylbenzamide reacts with 1. LiAlH4 in THF; 2. H2O to yield N,N-Dimethylbenzylamine (PhCH2N(CH3)2). Rationale: LiAlH4 reduces the amide carbonyl completely to a methylene group, preserving the amine functionality.

questions.chapter_title: Carboxylic Acid Derivatives: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution Reactions
questions.question: What is the expected major product when N-Boc-Alanine + Glycine methyl ester is treated with DCC (dicyclohexylcarbodiimide) in CH2Cl2?
questions.explanation: Treating N-Boc-Alanine + Glycine methyl ester with DCC (dicyclohexylcarbodiimide) in CH2Cl2 yields N-Boc-Alanylglycine methyl ester + DCU byproduct. Rationale: DCC activates the carboxylic acid as an O-acylisourea, facilitating nucleophilic attack by amine.
